name: B-lymphoblastic leukemia/lymphoma with t(17;19)(q22;p13)

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: WHO Classification of Tumors of Hematopoietic and Lymphoid Tissues (2022)

criteria.description: Presence of t(17;19)(q22;p13) chromosomal translocation resulting in E2A-HLF fusion gene
Immunophenotypic profile consistent with B-lymphoblastic leukemia/lymphoma (CD19+, CD10+, TdT+)
Bone marrow or peripheral blood blast count ≥20%
Morphologic features of lymphoblasts on peripheral blood or bone marrow smear

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Detection of t(17;19) translocation with compatible immunophenotype and blast count ≥20%
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Molecular confirmation of E2A-HLF fusion is critical due to aggressive clinical course.

pathognomonic.notes: Due to paraneoplastic secretion of PTHrP by leukemic cells
searchTerms: high blood calcium causing muscle twitching
muscle spasms due to calcium imbalance

pathognomonic.notes: Commonly observed at presentation in t(17;19) B-ALL
Manifests as anemia, thrombocytopenia, and neutropenia
searchTerms: bone marrow not producing enough blood cells
failure to make red, white cells and platelets

common.notes: Enlarged lymph nodes due to lymphomatous involvement
Enlargement of liver and spleen from leukemic infiltration

common.symptomName: Bone pain due to marrow expansion
common.notes: Common presenting symptom in pediatric patients
Often related to marrow failure or infection

occasional.symptomName: Central nervous system involvement symptoms (headache, cranial nerve palsies)
occasional.notes: Leukemic infiltration of CNS may occur
searchTerms: headache and nerve palsies from brain involvement
central nervous system symptoms including headache

occasional.symptomName: Respiratory distress due to mediastinal mass
occasional.notes: Rare but possible in lymphomatous presentations
searchTerms: shortness of breath due to mediastinal tumor

occasional.symptomName: Renal impairment secondary to leukemic infiltration or hypercalcemia
occasional.notes: May present with elevated creatinine or electrolyte abnormalities

searchTerms: losing weight and sweating at night

rare.notes: Rare skin manifestations of leukemic infiltration

rare.symptomName: Ophthalmological involvement (optic nerve infiltration, retinal hemorrhages)
rare.notes: Uncommon but reported in advanced disease

rare.symptomName: Psychiatric symptoms secondary to CNS involvement
searchTerms: psychiatric symptoms due to CNS disease

laboratory: Peripheral blood and bone marrow blasts ≥20%
Hypercalcemia with elevated serum calcium and PTHrP
Coagulopathy with elevated D-dimer and low fibrinogen
imaging: Chest X-ray or CT showing mediastinal mass or lymphadenopathy
Ultrasound or CT abdomen showing hepatosplenomegaly
other: Immunophenotyping showing B-cell markers CD19+, CD10+, TdT+
Bone marrow biopsy demonstrating lymphoblast infiltration

distinguishingFeatures: Presence of t(9;22)(q34;q11) BCR-ABL1 fusion gene
Less commonly associated with hypercalcemia or DIC

redFlags: Rapid onset of disseminated intravascular coagulation
Severe hypercalcemia refractory to standard treatment
Neurological deterioration indicating CNS leukemic infiltration
references: WHO Classification of Tumors of Hematopoietic and Lymphoid Tissues, 5th Edition, 2022
Pui CH, et al. Acute lymphoblastic leukemia. Lancet. 2012;379(9817):1502-1513.
Mullighan CG, et al. E2A-HLF fusion in B-lymphoblastic leukemia: clinical and biological features. Blood. 2002;99(3): 1022-1029.
